implementerProof.how: Round 6. The round's production delta is comment text alone, and that was checked rather than assumed: `git diff 9bb00ac9db1a 5b1049d8a40c -- 'packages/*' ':(exclude)*_test.go' ':(exclude)*.md'` with every `//` line filtered out prints nothing. The sentence it corrects is true of the code: issue_create.go:404-406 calls computeAndPersistSuggestions inside `if advice != nil`, after writeAdvice, so a fatal advice failure on a creation means LEGION-550's suggestions are never computed and no row is written — which is what my round-5 run already showed from the other side, the created issue keeping its suggestions once the walk's failure stopped being fatal. The one test change is TestClaimSurvivesAFailingLegionLabelWalk using rawClaimFields instead of its own inline decode. This pod was replaced before the round (new sandbox uid), so the rig was rebuilt from the issue volume and every lane restarted; both branch lanes were then proved to be running this head's binary by comparing sha256 of /proc/<pid>/exe with the built file (3fbabb1c941f2574… for 18877, 18879 and the file). Every row was driven again: verify.sh 67 assertions, break2.sh 13, boom.sh 31, and the four Go locks on the rig, all 0 failures.

correctionToEarlierRounds: One row of my own earlier evidence was vacuous and is fixed here rather than left standing. verify.sh's break row 'dispatch ask drops the line too' called `dispatch ask` with --context and --recommendation, flags the command does not take, so the CLI refused it with 'unknown flag' and the row asserted the absence of a line in a refusal. It now calls `dispatch ask --question …` and asserts, first, that the ask was really opened, and only then that the line is absent — which is why verify.sh is 67 assertions this round rather than 66. paneAnomaly: Reported to the architect and the implementer rather than pinned, since a wrong identity on a commit is a pane-environment problem (skill://legion-worker, and docs/solutions/legion/shared-main-repo-hazards-for-concurrent-issue-workspaces.md, Hazard 1): this round's code commit 284f41267c3a, `docs(dispatch): say what a fatal advice failure really costs a creation`, is authored by the **review** App (343353696+legion-reviewer[bot]) while its committer is the implement App and its Omp-Session trailer is the implementer's session 01a17025-15e6-75b1-953c-daf1a0d4c880. Author of one App and committer of another, in the implementing phase, is the signature of splitting the working-copy commit left by the previous role — here the reviewer's handoff c4d900ce60e3 — rather than running `jj new` first. Every other commit on the branch has its own role's App in both columns. It changes no behaviour and no gate refuses it; it is the branch's attribution that is wrong, and the architect decides whether a rewrite is worth it.
harnessNote: The pod replacement left the Postgres data directory on the issue volume group-writable (the volume is setgid), and Postgres refuses to start on anything but 0700 or 0750 — `data directory "/legion/scratch/harness/pgdata" has invalid permissions`. setup.sh now chmods it before starting, so the next pod needs no hand fix.
